record.paper_title: Some Open Questions in Quiver Gauge Theory
record.original_question: Is there a faster, algorithmic way to determine the generalized s-rule from dot diagrams, suitable for implementation in code without missing admissible tessellations?

evidence.quote: Question 8. Is there a faster way/(coding) algorithm to determine generalized s-rule using dot diagrams?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
In the context of five-dimensional supersymmetric gauge theories engineered by webs of (p,q)-five-branes with 7-branes, one encodes a brane configuration by a "dot diagram" (a planar arrangement of dots inside a polygon together with chosen partitions/colorings indicating how external legs terminate on 7-branes). The "generalized s-rule" is a combinatorial admissibility constraint on tessellations of such a dot diagram into sub-pieces (each corresponding to an irreducible component of the configuration), forbidding configurations in which more than a prescribed number of branes end on the same 7-brane in a way that would break supersymmetry; equivalently, it selects which decompositions of the dot diagram into colored sub-tessellations are physically admissible.

Problem. Design an algorithm that, given as input a dot diagram (the lattice polygon together with its internal/boundary dot data and 7-brane coloring), enumerates all tessellations of the diagram that satisfy the generalized s-rule, with the following properties:

(a) (Completeness) The algorithm must not miss any admissible tessellation.
(b) (Efficiency) The running time should be substantially faster than naive enumerate-and-filter approaches based on listing all tessellations and then checking the s-rule constraint case by case.
(c) (Implementability) The procedure must be explicit enough to be implemented as code, with a precise specification of the data structure for dot diagrams and a precise combinatorial reformulation of the generalized s-rule.

Either exhibit such an algorithm together with a proof of its correctness and a complexity bound, or prove that no algorithm with running time below a specified threshold can exist.
artifact.status_search_result: A targeted web search did not return any source presenting an explicit algorithmic enumeration of admissible dot-diagram tessellations under the generalized s-rule, nor a proof of impossibility. No follow-up work claiming to resolve this algorithmic question was located, so the current status is inconclusive.

status_evidence.title: Quiver diagram - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: General background on quiver diagrams in gauge theory; no algorithm for the generalized s-rule on dot diagrams is described.
status_evidence.claim: Standard references on quivers do not address an algorithmic generalized s-rule procedure.

status_evidence.title: N=2 Generalized Superconformal Quiver Gauge Theory (arXiv:1006.3486)
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses algorithms for determining duality-frame gauge content, but not the s-rule on dot diagrams.
status_evidence.claim: No directly relevant algorithm for the generalized s-rule appears in related quiver-gauge-theory algorithmic literature found.
